newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Feb 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Kirstie Marshall became Australia's first skiing world champion when she won the aerial gold medal at the world's freestyle championships in Nagano, Japan, yesterday. She demolished her own world record by 11 points to finish 20 points clear of her nearet competitors. Marshall had previously been a bronze medallist at the 1995 championships. Page 19.

Australian tennis Captain John Newcombe is confident of his teams prospects for regaining the Davis Cup after his team defeated the current championship holders France 4-1 in Sydney yesterday. Australia is next to meet either India or the Czech Republic in the quarter-final in April, before meeting the United States in September. Page 19.

Australian Syd Fischer confirmed at the weekend that he would be mounting a challenge for the America's Cup in Auckland in 2000. He has now equalled the British tea magnate Sir Thomas Lipton's five attempts at the title earlier this century. Fischer came closest to contesting the title in 1987 with his boat Steak'n'Kidney in Fremantle. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Last week Super League kicked off its championship with the World Nines. This weekend the Australian Rugby League launched its season with the World Sevens. Australia's two rival football leagues have now started their contest for the hearts and audiece of the Australian viewing public. Commentators agree that whichever proves the most financially successful this year will dominate the 1998 football competition. Page 27.

The Australian cricket team is considered to be the underdogs in the South African three-Test series which will be launched this week. Despite having successfully defended the Frank Worrell Trophy international, commentators believe that the South Africa team will prove invincible on their home turf. Both the Australian and West Indies cricket teams have displayed contrasting form this season, being both excellent and woeful alternately. Page 28.

Australian golf player Geoff Ogilvy made a welcome return to world class form yesterday at the Victorian Amateur golf championship final at the Commonwealth Golf Club in Melbourne yesterday. He is now looking forward to playing at this years Australian Open at Metropolitan, thanks to recent exemptions granted to Australian amateur champions. Page 29.
THE AGE

At the Victorian athletic championships held at Olympic Park, Melbourne, Emma George set a new world record in the pole vault with a vault measured at 4.50 metres. The win followed a shaky start in which she has struggled to clear 4.30 metres in two jump. Emma, who had just recovered from a hamstring injury a month earlier, is now a favourite for a gold medal at the world indoor championships to be held next month. Page 5.

Karla Gilbert, from the Queensland Gold Coast, won the Devondale Ironwoman championship series yesterday, making her the top of her sport in Australia. The 21 year old finished the season just one point short of a perfect score and with prize mony of A$44,253. She had been runner up in the series for the past two years. Page 12.

Commentators in Australia are divided on their opinion of the cricket team set to tour South Africa. Some say Australia has one of its best teams ever, while others say that their are serious long-term weakness both in the team and in Australian cricket generally. Both views can be supported by Australia's recent performance in which they have lost as many times as they have won, with three test matches won and three lost. Page 9.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian Cricket Board has requested that the Federal Government ensure that the upcoming Australian tour of South African is the last major series not shown live on free-to-air tv. The pay-TV network Foxtel is currently planning to broadcast the tour. It plans to offer a one hour package of highlights to the Seven network but commentators in Australia believe this is unlikely to satisfy the viewing public who are used to extensive coverage of tours on free-to-air television. Page 78.

Australian golf player Wayne Grady surrendered the South Australian Open golf title to New Zealander Steve Alker yesterday. In a dramatic finish at Kooyonga, Adelaide, Grady suffered a triple bogey on the second last hole. It was a traumatic loss for Grady who after performing well throughout the whole tournament was expected to win. Grady has not won a major tournament since the 1991 Australian PGA. Page 74.

World Cup champions Michael Klim and Adrian Radley set new state records in their events yesterday at the Victorian swimming championships. Klim shaved 0.42 seconds off his 1996 record in the 50m freestyle. This was only 0.21 seconds outside the Australin record. Radley set a state record in the 50m backstroke clocking up 26.25 seconds, just 0.01 seconds short of the Australian record. Page 74.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

A group of leading racing analysts have claimed that 10,000 jobs will be lost in the Australian racing industry, unless state governments change their discriminatory wage and tax policies. Among the reforms called for is a suggestion by Commercial Throughbred Breeders Association director John Messara that the industry by allowed to keep a greater share of the profits generated by TAB betting. Page 38.

Australian Davis Cup selectors will be able to choose from a host of singles players talent when Australia faces India or the Czech Republic in the next Davis Cup round at Memorial Drive, Adelaide. Contenders for inclusion in the team include Jason Stolenberg and Mark Philippoussis who have recovered from summer injuries. Page 35.

The Sydney United soccer team defeated South Melbourne last night 2-0 at Edensor Park, Melbourne. The win ensures that Sydney United will retain the Ericsson Cup minor premiership. The game was hard fought with Sydney United scoring goals by Robert Trjkovski and David Zdrillic. Page 34.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
